definition: LeNet is a series of convolutional neural network architectures created by a research group at AT&T Bell Laboratories between of the period of 1988 to 1998, centered around Yann LeCun.
details: They were designed for reading small grayscale images of handwritten digits and letters, and were used in ATMs for reading cheques. Convolutional neural networks are a kind of feed-forward neural network whose artificial neurons can respond to a part of the surrounding cells in the coverage range and perform well in large-scale image processing. LeNet-5 was one of the earliest convolutional neural networks and was historically important during the development of deep learning. In general, when LeNet is referred to without a number, it refers to the 1998 version, LeNet-5, which is the most well-known version.

explainer.lead: LeNet is a series of convolutional neural network architectures created at AT&T Bell Laboratories between 1988 and 1998, centered on Yann LeCun. LeNet-5 was one of the earliest CNNs and was historically important in the development of deep learning.

tiers.eli5: It's an early computer vision system that learned to read handwritten numbers by looking at small patches of an image, the way you'd recognize a digit by its strokes rather than memorizing the whole picture.
tiers.practitioner: The LeNet family was designed for reading small grayscale images of handwritten digits and letters, and was deployed in ATMs for reading cheques; CNNs are feed-forward networks whose neurons respond to part of the surrounding cells in their coverage range and perform well in large-scale image processing. A pitfall is assuming such early architectures scale unchanged to modern large-image tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: A series of convolutional neural network architectures (notably LeNet-5) built for small grayscale images; CNNs are feed-forward neural networks whose artificial neurons respond to a part of the surrounding cells in the coverage range.

explainer.example: LeNet-5 takes a small grayscale image of a handwritten digit and outputs its class; deployed in ATMs, it read handwritten characters on cheques.
